diagnose_vibration.overall_diagnosis: ISO Severity: Zone D (Unacceptable) — RMS velocity 53.75 mm/s. Dominant frequency: 30.0 Hz (shaft: 29.9 Hz). The strongest line of the spectrum is at 1.00 times the declared shaft frequency (within 10 % of 1x). Its dominance does not identify a fault, and it is not counted as a finding. This check cannot distinguish the 1x response of a machine in normal condition from unbalance, a bent or bowed rotor, eccentricity, misalignment, mechanical looseness or a soft foot, a worn or damaged coupling, a resonance near running speed, vibration transmitted from another machine, or a component at the electrical supply frequency, which lies close to 1x on a two-pole motor. Narrowing these down needs more than this check, such as a finer analysis of the line's frequency, a baseline from the same machine at the same condition, phase, a second radial or an axial channel, or several speeds. Establishing a cause needs a physical check of the machine. Another analysis that reads this same line of the same signal repeats the observation and does not corroborate it. Bearing analysis: The significance-tested evidence is inconclusive and does not support a unique fault type. Combined evidence across the analyses that ran: moderate. It counts findings, is not a probability, and does not identify or confirm a fault type.
recommendations: IMMEDIATE ACTION: Stop machine and inspect.
Bearing 6205: repeat the measurement, or compare it with a comparable earlier measurement.
